# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 5 (Bu-Vb Sk5)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk5  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 5  
**Title (English, from literature):** Being unrestrained  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali. All secondary literature passages retrieved under the designation "sk 5" are false matches referring to non-Vinaya treatises, notably the *Sāṁkhyakārikā* and the *Mahāyānasangraha*.

The rule is extensively paralleled across the canonical codes of early Buddhist schools. Within the Pali Vinaya, exact counterparts exist in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk5*), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk5*), the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (*pli-tv-bi-pm-sk5*), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī *Parivāra* (*Sekhiya* 5). Across other traditions, parallel rules are preserved in the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya (attested in Chinese translations and Sanskrit manuscript fragments), the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya (extant in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit), the Mahīśāsaka Vinaya (Chinese), the Mahāsāṅghika and Lokottaravāda traditions (Sanskrit), and the Kāśyapīya Vinaya.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
